articles.title: Scottish Premiership: Durán caps Celtic’s comeback win over Hibernian
articles.summary: Hibernian 1-2 Celtic; Rangers 4-0 St Johnstone. Kevin Kelsy scores two to sink 10-man Saints. Camilo Durán moved into double figures for the season as Celtic reasserted themselves at the top of the Premiership by coming from behind to defeat beleaguered Hibernian 2-1 at windy Easter Road.
body: After another Europa League setback at home to Celta Vigo on Thursday, the champions bounced back with a victory that restored their four-point cushion over Rangers at the top. The home side, who are bottom, took an early lead through Owen Elding but it was swiftly cancelled out by a Jason Kerr own goal before Duran’s 10th of the season edged the visitors ahead just before the break.
It proved enough to secure a ninth win in 10 league games and ensure the recently appointed home boss, Marink Reedijk, suffered a third straight defeat since succeeding David Gray.

There were a couple of blemishes for Celtic, however, as substitute Alistair Johnston’s return from injury lasted barely 20 minutes before he had to go off, while £11million forward Kasper Hogh – restored to the starting line-up after notching in just one of his 13 previous matches for the Hoops – again drew a blank before being replaced in the 64th minute.

articles.title: Russia to host first Olympic federation world event since Ukraine invasion
articles.summary: The International Weightlifting Federation becomes the first Olympic federation to choose Russia to host a world championships since its invasion of Ukraine.
body: Moscow will host the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships - the first time an Olympic federation has chosen to stage a global event in Russia since the country's invasion of Ukraine began in 2022.
The International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) announced its decision on Sunday, four months after confirming Russian athletes would again be eligible to compete in its events.
In July, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) provisionally lifted a suspension on the Russian Olympic Committee.
The IOC's subsequent decision potentially opened the way for Russian athletes to compete for their country at the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

articles.title: Osaka 'not far off' her best but often ponders future
articles.summary: Four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka says she is returning to her best form but would consider quitting the game if asked to by her three-year-old daughter.
body: Naomi Osaka says she is "not far off" the form that saw her win four Grand Slam titles, but admits she has thought about quitting and often ponders her future.
The 29-year-old Japanese star twice won both the US Open and Australian Open, between 2018 and 2021, during a glittering start to her career that saw her rise to number one in the world.
But she took time out of the sport in 2021 to prioritise her mental health and another 15 months away after becoming pregnant, before returning in 2023 following the birth of her daughter.
Osaka now says that she would quit tennis if her three-year-old, Shai, asked her to, despite climbing back up the world rankings and once again challenging for major titles.

articles.title: What Chelsea Did Wrong vs Tottenham
articles.summary: After a stellar run following the international break, things came crashing down for Chelsea as they lost 2-0 to Tottenham Hotspur at the weekend. This marked an extremely rare defeat at Stamford Bridge to the Lilywhites, a crack in a strong record of home wins that has left fans reeling.
body: The average positions for the Blues team shows a very erratic unit, it was entirely different to the rigid 3-4-3 of the season opener and the fluid destruction from the win over Everton. Notably, there were large gaps that went unfilled, with Moises Caicedo and Jordan Henderson lower while Cole Palmer was high, Pedro Neto was totally isolated out on the right.

The left-hand side was far less convoluted than it was against the Toffees. In that game, Morgan Rogers, Joao Pedro, and Jorrel Hato were almost one tight blob on the average position map. For this fixture, it was much more isolated with the left back staying deeper, Geovany Quenda coming in and occupying a left midfield space, while Rogers drifted a bit to that side.

There was no central penetration offered, it was a system that tried to put three players high and space them out but it resulted in a failure to progress the ball, leaving Chelsea with very little of the possession, and even fewer ideas to break down a strong line.
